title: How Ultraviolet Light Reaches You and How to Block It
post_title: How Ultraviolet Light Reaches You and How to Block It | QuantaTale
post_description: What ultraviolet radiation is, how the atmosphere filters it and how to protect your skin, from the CDC and WHO. Sources: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention https://www.cdc.gov/skin-cancer/sun-safety/index.html and World Health Organization https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/radiation-ultraviolet-(uv) #Science #ScienceFacts #QuantaTale
narration: Can you get sunburnt on a cloudy day? Ultraviolet rays are invisible radiation from the sun, and they can damage skin cells. The atmosphere absorbs all UVC and most UVB, but it filters UVA much less. So most of the UV that reaches the ground is UVA. UV is strongest when the sun is high, because then its rays travel the most direct route to Earth. Higher up there is less air to absorb it, so UV is stronger on a mountain than at sea level. UV also gets through on cloudy, cool days, and it bounces off water, sand and snow. Wear broad-spectrum sunscreen rated SPF 15 or higher before going outside. The best sunglasses block both UVA and UVB.
